title: Do Dogs Dream? Here's What Science Says

script: If you've ever watched your dog's paws twitch and their eyes move while they're asleep, that's not just muscle spasms, dogs really do dream. Their brains go through the same sleep cycles ours do, including REM sleep, the stage where most dreaming happens. Researchers studying brain activity in sleeping dogs found patterns almost identical to humans dreaming. And based on studies of rats replaying their day's maze runs during sleep, scientists believe dogs likely dream about their day too, chasing squirrels, playing fetch, maybe even you. Smaller dogs tend to dream more often but for shorter bursts, while bigger dogs dream less frequently but longer. So that little sleep-run happening on your couch right now is probably a full replay of their favorite park.
